newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr pauses at close after break above US$0.70.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr pauses at close after break above US$0.70.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar paused for breath after smashing through US$0.70 to reach an eight year high just three and a half weeks before a general election, but remained well bid at Wednesday's close.
The currency traded up to US$0.7012 and 66.74 on its Trade-Weighted Index before settling back to 0.6992/99 and 66.65 at the close.

Dealers said the market continued to shrug off uncertainty surrounding the October 12 election, in which the conservative government is threatened by three left-wing parties collectively drawing more than 50 percent support in opinion polls.
"The demand from euro issues, samurai bond issues etc is too strong for any worries on that to dampen the kiwi," an Auckland trader said.

A senior Wellington dealer said Japanese retail interest in the form of samurais was the main factor behind the break above 0.70, but the Kiwi ran into offers around 0.7010 and drifted off as the trader market was caught long on the day.
A weaker Australian dollar also acted as a drag on the currency. But Kiwi's retracement had been modest, and it still looked very well bid.

"A lot of people have tried selling the currency and that hasn't worked in the face of just the sheer volume of retail NZ dollar issues that are going through the market at the moment, both out of Japan and out of Europe," the dealer said.
Resistance around 0.7010 was seen as critical.

Barring any serious political ructions, any move lower would be a grind. "It's hard to see it moving down in any sort of aggressive manner. I think there's going to be buyers all the way down in the currency," he said.
